svg.text: TRANSFER automation script for Azure Key Vault certificates in DigiCert TLM
What the script does today, and the ways it can be driven once the manual Common Name entry is replaced by policy
WHO OR WHAT RUNS THE SCRIPT
SCRIPT FLOW (bash · curl + jq · TLM ui-api)
Runs the bash script from a workstation. Picks a Common
Name or list number, reviews the payload and confirms.
Exactly what the script does now.
Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions or GitLab job on a schedule or
on demand. Non-interactive mode, TLM API key from pipeline
secrets, results in the job log.
Script packaged as a small image (curl + jq). Azure
Container Apps job, AKS CronJob or Docker on a schedule.
Secrets via Key Vault reference or environment.
Same logic in PowerShell as a scheduled runbook. Managed
Identity, TLM API key in Key Vault or Automation variables.
Hybrid worker if TLM is reached privately.
Polls the TLM inventory on a schedule and selects by
policy: expiring in < N days, issuer is not DigiCert, self-
signed, or tagged. Submits TRANSFER with no CN typed by
NewVersionCreated) → Azure Function or Logic App → script.
Notifications to Teams, e-mail or ITSM.
Keep only records whose automation_action primary or secondary
action is TRANSFER, then sort by Common Name.
Manual: CN or list number (PoC). Automatic: policy-driven choice
fed by the monitor, pipeline or event (expiry, issuer, tags).
action_type TRANSFER · cn · sans (CN removed) · profile_id
POST /ui-api/v1/automation with x-api-key. Confirmation prompt when
HTTP status and response JSON → console, pipeline log or runbook
output; optional webhook to Teams, e-mail or ITSM.
interactive mode loops: automate another → re-discover
automation inventory, filtered by connector / account, paged
creates the TRANSFER automation and runs it now
picks the sensor, calls the connector plugin
from the record, or DEFAULT_PROFILE_ID in the script
built by jq from the selected inventory record
record CN; SANs minus the CN
off for the PoC (enable to let TLM renew)
extensibility plugin on a TLM sensor → one vault
TLM runs the connector for the TRANSFER: a new version of the same
certificate object is created in the vault, the CSR is signed by
DigiCert and the chain merged back. The private key never leaves Azure.
Self-signed or third-party certificate sits in the vault. The connector
discovers it into the TLM inventory and flags it TRANSFER-eligible.
The script, or any trigger above, submits the automation. TLM runs the
connector: new version in the vault, CSR signed by DigiCert, chain merged
The object is DigiCert-issued and TLM-managed. With auto-renew on, TLM
renews it ahead of expiry through the same connector, with no manual
